newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil's Europipe II gas line gets go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Statoil's Europipe II gas line gets go-ahead.

text.p: Norway's parliament has approved plans for the installation and operation of the Europipe II gas trunkline from Kaarstoe, north of Stavanger, to Germany, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.
Statoil said its proposed route across the island of Bokn from the gas treatment plant at Kaarstoe to the North Sea won support from parliament, or the Storting.
"We're very pleased the Storting approved this choice," Kenneth Engervik, Europipe II procurement manager, told Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter.
Owned by 11 oil companies and operated by Statoil, the trunkline will come ashore at Dornum on the north German coast.
The 635 kilometre line is due to begin operating in October 1999 at a cost of around 6.8 billion crowns.
